subject: Recap & next steps — FinSet privacy & data access playbook
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Patil <rajiv.patil@finset.com>, Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@finset.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — FinSet privacy & data access playbook

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick written recap and concrete next steps so we can align with your security and product teams. TL;DR: Redwood can meet FinSet's core asks (PII handling, configurable retention, tenant isolation, RBAC + break-glass) but we need a few inputs from you to firm up the pilot configuration.

Summary of what we covered:
- PII classification & redaction: can apply prompt-side redaction + token-level suppression at the ingestion layer.
- Retention: default short-term logs (30 days), configurable embeddings retention separately; archival options available for audit-only storage.
- Logging & observability: per-request audit logs (request id, model, route, user id) with configurable retention and export to your SIEM.
- Data residency & tenancy: hosted (multi-tenant), Dedicated (isolated GPU pools), and Private (VPC / on-prem) options; encryption keys can be customer-managed (KMS/HSM).
- Support access / break-glass: break-glass processes exist — emergency operator actions are logged, require pre-approved workflows and time-limited session tokens.
- RBAC: role templates (admin, ops, support-readonly, support-elevated) + ability to scope to projects/accounts.

Requested items / next steps (action owners):
1) Alex (me): share SOC2 summary + architecture diagram + access-matrix template (attached). Target: EOD today.
2) FinSet: confirm desired retention windows for embeddings vs. raw payloads and whether you require customer-managed KMS for pilot. Target: before follow-up call.
3) Redwood security (cc Laura): prepare break-glass runbook and short note on audit retention we support. Target: pre-call.
4) Schedule 30-min follow-up with FinSet security (proposed: Tue Jul 20 10:00 PT).

Attachments: SOC2_summary_redwood_v2.pdf, redwood_architecture_finset_view.png, access_matrix_template.xlsx

If that matches your read, can you confirm 10:00 PT Tuesday for a focused security + infra session?

— Alex Martinez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Patil <rajiv.patil@finset.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@finset.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — FinSet privacy & data access playbook

Thanks Alex — useful recap. A couple quick clarifying questions before the call:

1) Retention: when you say embeddings are configurable separately, what are the minimum and maximum retention windows supported out-of-the-box? We need a 90-day default for embeddings but want the option to reduce to 7 days for certain projects.
2) Encryption: do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) in a Dedicated deployment, and can we integrate with our AWS KMS policy for key rotation?
3) Support access: can you provide a short written assurance that support access is role-limited and requires both an approval ticket and time-limited session? We’ll need that for our compliance gate.

Please include security@finset.com on the follow-up invite; I’ll loop them if needed.

— Rajiv
Director of Product, FinSet Analytics
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Patil <rajiv.patil@finset.com>, Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@finset.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 18:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — FinSet privacy & data access playbook

Great questions — quick answers inline and attaching the short docs you can circulate.

1) Retention windows for embeddings:
- Min: 0 days (ephemeral) — we can auto-delete on ingest.
- Typical presets: 7 / 30 / 90 / 365 days.
- Max: indefinite archival to your storage (audit-only) if requested; we can export to your S3 with lifecycle rules.
So 90-day default is supported; we’ll highlight per-project overrides in the access matrix.

2) Encryption / CMK:
- Supported: customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private.
- Key rotation: yes — we integrate with AWS KMS policies and support rotation; for HSM-backed keys we can plug into common providers via KMIP.

3) Support access & approvals:
- Short assurance: Support access is role-based and requires a documented approval ticket for any privileged actions; elevated sessions are time-limited and recorded in audit logs (immutable).
- We’ll attach a short break-glass runbook for the call.

I’ve attached: SOC2_summary_redwood_v2.pdf, redwood_architecture_finset_view.png, access_matrix_template.xlsx. Also linking our private deployment guide: https://redwood.app/docs/private-deployments

I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue Jul 20 10:00 PT — does that work for you and your security team?

— Alex
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Patil <rajiv.patil@finset.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Break-glass / emergency access — brief runbook

Hi Rajiv — Vivek from Redwood security here. Wanted to drop the high-level controls we enforce so you have a crisp artefact for your compliance folks before the call.

- Preconditions: break-glass is only available for predefined emergency scopes (data-recovery, service-restoration). All requests must reference a Jira ticket or PagerDuty incident id.
- Approvals: two-person approval for any elevation (team lead + on-call security engineer). Approvals recorded in our approval ledger.
- Sessions: time-limited ephemeral credentials (default 15 minutes), explicit justification required in the ticket.
- Auditing: every elevated session produces an immutable audit record (who, scope, commands, start/end timestamps). Audit records retained per your retention policy (configurable; default 1 year).
- Post-incident: post-mortem and revoke confirmation required; access tokens are revoked immediately after session end.

We’ll bring a draft playbook to the call (attached in the thread) and can modify retention and approval windows to match FinSet policy. Can you confirm what your audit retention window needs to be for elevated session records?

— Vivek Kulkarni
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Patil <rajiv.patil@finset.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@finset.com>, security@finset.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Break-glass / emergency access — brief runbook

Thanks Vivek — that level of detail helps. Quick follow-ups before the call:

- Please send a single-paragraph statement we can include in our compliance packet that says Redwood enforces role-based support access, requires approval tickets, and records time-limited elevated sessions in immutable audit logs.
- For the access-matrix: we need a completed draft from Redwood by EOD next Monday (Jul 26) so our InfoSec can review before the pilot. Can you confirm feasibility?
- Also include the SLA for support access response times during the pilot (we’ll evaluate this for enterprise SLA later).

I’ll join the 10:00 PT call. Please include a calendar invite to security@finset.com.

— Rajiv
